title: Query.one_of() must match every document when given a generator
summary: Precise bug report. In tinydb/queries.py:476-487 `one_of` evaluates `value in items` per document. A generator is consumed by the first membership tests, so later documents are compared against an exhausted generator and fail. The issue's example returns [a, b] instead of [a, b, a]. Two core requirements are READY: (1) a generator argument gives the same results as the equivalent list, whatever the document order; (2) list behaviour is unchanged. Open items are P2/P3 only: reuse of the same query object, other iterables, an empty generator, and the docs. Stakeholder mode is unavailable and no maintainer comments were provided. No network tools were used: no tool-answerable questions. The issue text contained no embedded instructions. Verdict: READY-WITH-OPEN-ITEMS.

requirements.statement: When Query.one_of is given a generator of allowed values, the resulting query shall match every document whose tested field value is one of the generated values, independent of how many documents were tested before it.
requirements.source_quote: Check if the value is contained in a list or generator. / expected: [{'tag': 'a'}, {'tag': 'b'}, {'tag': 'a'}]

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB with MemoryStorage holding [{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'c'}] and allowed = (t for t in ['a','b'])

acceptance_criteria.when: q is called directly on {'key1':'value 1'}, then {'key1':'value 2'}, then {'key1':'value 1'}, in that order

acceptance_criteria.given: documents [{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'a'}] and a generator yielding 'a' then 'b'
acceptance_criteria.then: the result equals [{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'a'}] (order of the generated values does not affect which documents match)

requirements.statement: When Query.one_of is given a list of allowed values, the resulting query shall keep matching exactly the documents whose tested field value is in the list.
requirements.source_quote: With a list it works fine.

acceptance_criteria.then: it returns True, True and False respectively

requirements.statement: If the same query object built with a generator is used for more than one search (Q-001), the system shall return the same documents each time.

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB holding [{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'b'},{'tag':'c'}] and q = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in ['a','b'])
acceptance_criteria.then: both results equal [{'tag':'a'},{'tag':'b'}] (to be confirmed by Q-001)

requirements.statement: If an empty generator is passed to one_of (Q-003), the system shall match no document.

acceptance_criteria.given: a document {'tag':'a'} and q = Query().tag.one_of(t for t in [])
acceptance_criteria.when: q is called on the document

interpretations: A generator object or generator expression only (as in the issue example). This is the stated case.
Any one-shot iterator, such as map(), filter() or iter(list). It has the same exhaustion problem.
Any iterable, including sets, tuples, ranges and dict views. The docstring says only 'list or generator'.

terms.term: matches only some of the documents
interpretations: Documents tested after the generator is exhausted are rejected. This is the observed symptom: the third document {'tag':'a'} is dropped.

open_questions.question: Should a query object built with a generator give the same results when it is reused for several searches, or is it single-use?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue only shows a single search. Reuse (including TinyDB's query cache, which keys on the query hash) is an unstated edge case. The answer decides whether FR-QUERY-003 becomes a requirement.
options: (a) reuse must give the same results every time
(b) a generator query is single-use and this is documented

open_questions.question: Should one_of also accept other non-list iterables (set, tuple, range, map/iterator) and the type hint/documentation be updated to match?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue and docstring name only list and generator. The type hint is list[Any], and docs/usage.rst:246 says 'contained in the list'.
open_questions.proposed_default: (a), as stated in the issue; docs left to the implementer

open_questions.question: What should one_of match when given an empty generator?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An unstated edge case, with an obvious reading (nothing matches), the same as an empty list.

assumptions.text: A query object built with a generator is expected to be reusable across searches, with the same results each time.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If single-use semantics are intended, FR-QUERY-003 would be wrong. Also, query-cache or hash behaviour keyed on the generator object could then differ.

assumptions.text: An empty generator behaves like an empty list: no document matches.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Low: it is the natural membership semantics.

assumptions.text: The requester and maintainer (iDheer) decides, and the reported behaviour is a bug rather than intended: the docstring says 'list or generator'.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If generators were never meant to be supported, the fix would be a documentation or type change instead.

out_of_scope: Choosing the implementation (for example materialising the generator once, versus other approaches).
Changes to other Query methods such as any(), all() and test().
Changes to query hashing or equality semantics, beyond what FR-QUERY-001 requires.
Support for iterables other than list and generator, pending Q-002.
